title: mixing_valve.emitter_delivery returns negative heat: a cold tank behind the valve cools the zones
claim: mixing_valve.emitter_delivery returns ua*(mix-zone) without its documented max(0, .) floor, so in the scalar two-zone throttled step a tank colder than a zone draws heat back out of the slab/upper floor into the tank, while the batch twin floors it at 0: 3674 two-zone valve trajectory elements differ even with D2-s1-01 corrected. On the 9 valved golden plans the scalar step booked 496 negative deliveries moving 87.52 kWh from the zones back into the tank (valve_storage_small_tank alone 57.3 kWh).
mechanism: mixing_valve.py:138 `return ua * (mix_temp - zone_temp)` under a docstring 'Never negative: a valve can shut, but it cannot cool a house'. _valve_two_zone_delivery uses it for q_rad and q_floor; simulate_trajectory_batch writes np.maximum(0.0, ...) for the same terms. Below the zone temperature the scalar model runs the emitters as a heat pump in reverse, booking zone heat into the tank (balance still closes, so conservation does not see it).

evidence.unit: mismatched trajectory elements (two-zone valve arms, lift corrected)
evidence.machine: box B4, 4 vCPU container, py3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: two other seats on the box; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --fix-emitter: mixing_valve.emitter_delivery swapped in memory for max(0.0, ua*(mix_temp-zone_temp))

metric_definition: Count of trajectory elements where the two-zone valved batch twin differs by any bit from the scalar path, with the lift factor corrected in both runs.
phenomenon_property: No emitter circuit delivers negative heat: behind a valve the zones are never cooled by the tank, in the scalar step and the batch twin alike.

null_control.value: single-zone valve arms (which floor drawn with np.maximum in _single_valve_rates): 0
null_control.note: the single-zone valve law floors its own draw, so its arms stay in parity

proposed_fix_scope: mixing_valve.py emitter_delivery: return max(0.0, ua * (mix_temp - zone_temp)).
